# Jubilees Chapter 46 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** The Joseph era ends; Israel's explosive growth; the new Pharaoh fears them

---

**46:1** After Jacob died, the family of Israel kept growing in Egypt — more and more people, stronger and stronger, until the land was full of them.

**46:2** Pharaoh died. Egypt mourned him for days. Then a new Pharaoh took power — a man who had never heard of Joseph.

**46:3** Joseph's brothers began to worry: "With Father gone, Joseph might finally take his revenge." They got word to Joseph: "Father left a message: forgive your brothers. Let go of what they did."

**46:4** The message reduced Joseph to tears. When his brothers came in and threw themselves at his feet, he could barely speak. "Don't be afraid," he said. "I'm not God. You had bad intentions toward me — but God had good intentions through you. Look at where we are now: lives saved, a nation fed. Don't be afraid. I will take care of you and your children."

**46:5** Joseph lived fifty-five more years after his father's death. He died at a hundred and ten.

**46:6** Before he died he made his sons promise: "When I go, take my bones back to Canaan." They swore it.

**46:7** Then Joseph's brothers died too — Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Dan, Gad, Asher, Naphtali — all of Jacob's sons died in Egypt. Jubilees dates this to the fiftieth year of the fiftieth jubilee.

**46:8** But the people kept growing. Israel was fruitful and multiplying and spreading across the land.

**46:9** The new Pharaoh watched this growth and felt the fear rise in him. He pulled his officials together: "We have to handle these Israelites carefully. They're already huge in number. If war breaks out, they could side with our enemies. We'd lose everything."

**46:10** They imposed forced labor. Taskmasters were appointed to work the Israelites hard. They built Pithom and Raamses for Pharaoh's storehouses. But the harder Pharaoh pushed, the more the people grew.

---

*PNEUMA notes: The transition from Genesis to Exodus (vv.2-3) is smoothly handled in Jubilees. Joseph's speech (v.4) is one of the most theologically profound passages in the entire Joseph cycle. The new Pharaoh's fear (vv.9-10) sets up the Exodus narrative of chapters 47-48.*
